sense_problem: 'have fitted' also fits (less natural with 'all week'); 'are going to fit' is not one word-gap but also possible

instruction_problem: 'Write one word in each gap' does not say which verb; 'must be' / 'can be' (less natural) also work, so more than one answer.

level_problem: Stative vs progressive contrast is well below C1 (B1/B2 point); a B1 learner solves it by instinct.

answer: He considers taking early retirement next year.
sense_problem: Option 4 is not clearly wrong: 'considers' in simple present is possible in some contexts (habitual/general), so the 'mistake' depends on reading it as a plan; ambiguous.

other_correct: You are constantly changing your mind.
instruction_problem: Unclear who speaks and what to say: 'Answer with' does not say the answer is a comment/complaint about the speaker; tense not specified so simple present is also correct. Learner cannot know a progressive is wanted.
level_problem: Fine for C1 only if the annoyed-habit nuance is clear; as worded it is guesswork.

instruction_problem: 'will usually be driving' is also correct (two words in the second gap).

answer: My neighbour forever is borrowing my tools.
sense_problem: Word-order error 'forever is borrowing' is a form few learners would write at C1; the wrong sentence is easy to spot.

answer: you're constantly interrupting me when I'm speaking
other_correct: when I'm speaking you're constantly interrupting me
you're interrupting me constantly when I'm speaking
constantly you're interrupting me when I'm speaking
instruction_problem: Task is just ordering seven given words; the meaning is already in the cards and the 'when' clause order is open, so several orders are correct. No hint which clause starts.
level_problem: Too easy for C1: only word order, no choice of form.
